name: security-audit-skill
description: A coding-agent skill for multi-phase security audits with independently verified, machine-readable findings
one_liner: Turns an AI coding assistant into a structured security auditor: it hunts for vulnerabilities in a codebase, double-checks its own findings with a second AI 'skeptic', and produces a clean report instead of a pile of unverified guesses.
buyer: A small-to-mid-size software company's engineering lead who needs a security review before a client audit or compliance deadline but can't afford a full outside pentest firm yet.
business_use_cases: A startup runs it before a SOC 2 audit to catch and fix obvious vulnerabilities cheaply, ahead of hiring an outside auditor.
A freelance security consultant uses it to do the first-pass grunt work on client codebases, then layers their own expert judgment on top, taking on more clients per month.
An agency building client software adds 'AI-assisted security pass' as a standard, billable step before every client handoff.

money_ideas.idea: Offer 'AI-assisted security audit' as a fixed-price service for startups too small to afford a traditional pentest.
Run it as a subscription CI check that re-audits a client's codebase on every release.

steal_this: Run it against three open-source or freemium products you use, write up the real (responsibly disclosed) findings as a public case study, then pitch the same audit as a paid service to non-technical founders who are nervous about security but can't afford Big Audit Firm rates.
